PASS: PASS (round 1). Audited HEAD 6f2892d. The working tree is clean. The sprint diff is b9ac6df..HEAD.

SPRINT FILE: I re-read it fresh before this verdict. The only change since Master Controller wrote it (b9ac6df) is the lifecycle-owned status line. No criterion compares two versions.

R1 met. "## CI commands" is gone and "## Local validation" replaces it. grep for "ci-commands" and "## CI commands" across the repo, excluding node_modules, .next and .git, finds nothing outside the sprint files.

R2 met. Tier 1 lists npm ci, lint, typecheck, test, build. That is ci.yml's build job (Install, Lint, Typecheck, Test, Build) step for step, and every script exists in package.json with the stated meaning. The README says npm run test excludes supabase/tests/**, which matches vitest.config.ts. It says next/font/google needs the network at build time; app/layout.tsx imports from next/font/google. The "what passing shows / what it doesn't" paragraph is accurate.

R3 met. Tier 2 lists supabase start, the env export, test:rls, then stop. That matches the rls-tests job, including CI's own "Export local stack URL/anon key" step. The README adapts that step for a shell by using grep for the two variables and stripping quotes with tr. The claim "without that line every test fails with 'Supabase client requires NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY'" agrees with lib/supabase/config.ts's exact throw text. vitest.rls.config.ts loads no env, and supabase/tests has no dotenv or loadEnv. The section links to #running-the-policy-tests instead of repeating it, and the anchor slug is correct.
One minor difference, not a finding: locally it uses npx supabase (devDependency ^2.114.0), while CI uses setup-cli "latest". The section calls tier 2 "the local equivalent", not "the same binary", so it is accurate.

R4 met. Every no-env claim agrees with the code:
- "/" gives 307: next.config.ts redirects with permanent:false.
- /chart needs no env: page.tsx is unchanged and does no database work on GET (Sprint 25 R6).
- Save fails with a 500 and Next's generic error: saveReading calls createAnonClient, which throws in resolvePublicConfig, and /chart has no error boundary.
- /reading/<id> gives 500 with the "temporarily unavailable" page: page.tsx's createAnonClient throws, and the route-wide error.tsx (eyebrow "Temporarily unavailable") catches it.
- /api/health/db gives 503 with status "misconfigured" and the admin client's exact message text, plus commit {sha:"local-dev", isLocal:true}: this is the health route's createAdminClient catch branch plus getDeployedCommit's LOCAL_FALLBACK_SHA when VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA is unset.
None of these claims disagrees with the code. The rendered text "This page couldn't load" is observed output I can't verify statically; LiveQA's fresh-clone pass covers it.

R5 met. The CI-only list matches the migrate job exactly: it needs build and rls-tests and runs only on a push to main; then link, db push, the drift check (db diff --linked), and the deploy hook. All four secrets are named correctly. The closing caveat is correct: tier 2 proves the migrations apply from scratch, not on top of production or that production hasn't drifted.

R6 met. One paragraph says the local-stack .env.local is the normal one. It says a production one means npm run dev and npm run start read and write production, to use it deliberately, and to delete it afterwards. Both are true: Next loads .env.local for dev and start alike.

R7: audited from the evidence I have. I did not see Dev Team's handoff text in this session. The commit message says every command was run as written with .env.local moved aside. The evidence on disk supports that. The project's local Supabase Docker volume (supabase_db_my_little_raccoon) was created at 2026-10-04T22:18:13Z, four minutes after sprint_started (22:14:51Z), and supabase/.temp/start-secrets is dated the same window. So Docker was started and tier 2 really ran during this build; the section's claim that tier 2 was verified is backed. .env.local is present with its untouched 27 Sep mtime, so it was moved back, not modified. If the handoff the user holds contradicts any of this, tell me and I will re-audit.

R8 met. Outside README.md and docs/sprints/, nothing changed. There is no version bump.

CI: lint 0, typecheck 0, tests 198/198 across 20 files, build 0.

ROUTE TO MASTER CONTROLLER (not a condition on this sprint): Dev Team found that the existing "### Running the policy tests" recipe fails as written. It omits the env export, and Vitest doesn't load .env.local. Out of Scope correctly kept that edit out of this sprint, and the new section documents the gap in place of fixing it. That leaves a known-broken two-line recipe in the README, sitting directly above the section that says it is broken. That needs its own follow-up, otherwise it becomes "known" by repetition. Also for MC: npm run build needs the network because of next/font/google at build time. The README now says so; whether that is acceptable is MC's call.

No test named known-failing. No new Human Prerequisites beyond the sprint's own: Supabase must be unpaused when Pipeman pushes.

Handoff: Dev Team runs /sprint-dev-done 26. LiveQA owns CI green including migrate, the health commit matching the push, and following the rendered README literally on a fresh clone.
commit=6f2892d | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 6f2892d2d471ef1edac44c558cc13c8f186c0ec4 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). Tested 2026-10-13. I followed the README exactly as GitHub renders it, on
a fresh clone with no .env.local. Tools: gh CLI for CI, curl, and headless Chromium
(Playwright) for browser-rendered claims.

PIPELINE CHECK, PASS.
CI is green on both pushed commits, all three jobs:
- 6f2892d: run 38392342021, build / rls-tests / migrate all success.
- db5ac58 (bookkeeping): run 38392859832, the same.
migrate's real steps ran, not skipped, in both runs: Link project, Push migrations,
Check for schema drift, Trigger production deployment, every one success.
/api/health/db: status "ok", connected true, migrationVersion
20260823004820_set_reading_horoscope.

One correction to the handoff paste. It says production reports 6f2892d. Live production
reports commit.sha db5ac5895d06f8f6902e6981ab21783ba2b24a31 (db5ac58), the bookkeeping tip
Pipeman also pushed. git diff --stat 6f2892d db5ac58 touches only
docs/sprints/state/sprint-26.json, so production is serving 6f2892d's content. The criterion
("commit.sha equal to the pushed commit") is met by the tip that was actually pushed.

README FOLLOWED LITERALLY, PASS.
Source: GitHub's rendered README via
gh api repos/samcollins9/my_little_racoon/readme (html media type), ref main. Each command
was taken verbatim from that page's rendered pre blocks, not retyped from memory.
Clone: a fresh git clone from origin at db5ac58. Its only env file is .env.example, and my
shell had zero inherited NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE / SUPABASE / VERCEL variables (and I unset them
explicitly as well).

Tier 1, all exit 0. Actual times vs the README's stated ones:
- npm ci: 10.1s (stated ~10s)
- npm run lint: 1.9s (~2s)
- npm run typecheck: 1.7s (~2s)
- npm run test: 1.1s (~1s), 198 passed (198)
- npm run build: 5.2s (~5s)

Running the built app locally: I ran the rendered line verbatim on the same clone, with no
.env.local:
  npm run build && npm run start   # http://localhost:3000
- "/ redirects (307) to /chart": matches. HTTP 307 -> http://localhost:3000/chart.
- /chart: matches. HTTP 200, date form present. /chart?date=1969-07-20 is HTTP 200 with
  "Positions calculated for" rendered.
- "See the full reading fails... returns 500... This page couldn't load": matches, 3/3 reps
  in a browser. The POST returned 500 and the page showed verbatim "This page couldn't load /
  A server error occurred. Reload to try again. / Reload / ERROR 661287365". The server log
  shows the cause: "Supabase client requires NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and
  NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY".
- "/reading/<any id> returns 500 with the temporarily unavailable page": matches in a browser
  for /reading/abc and a real uuid. Both are HTTP 500, showing "TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE /
  This reading can't be shown right now. / Something went wrong on our side. Try this link
  again in a few minutes." The phrase is client-rendered; it is not in curl's raw HTML.
- /api/health/db: matches the README character for character. HTTP 503,
  {"status":"misconfigured","connected":false,"migrationVersion":null,"error":"Supabase admin
  client requires NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY",
  "commit":{"sha":"local-dev","short":"local-dev","isLocal":true}}.
I stopped the local server afterwards, killing only the PID whose cwd was my clone.

TIER 2: run. It is not part of the gate, but Docker was up (engine 29.7.2), so I ran it.
I ran the rendered block verbatim as one bash script on the clone: supabase start, the
export line, npm run test:rls, supabase stop. Exit 0, 33s total.
- The export set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321 plus the local demo anon key.
- test:rls: Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 10 passed (10).
- The stack stopped cleanly.

FINDING, LOW (README wording, not a blocker). I checked the claim "Without that line, every
test fails with Supabase client requires NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY" by running test:rls with the stack up but no export.
The exact message is right, but the failure is at file load, not per test. Output:
"Test Files 2 failed (2)", "Tests no tests", and the error
"Supabase client requires NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY" twice,
once per file. "Both test files fail to load with..." would be literal. Someone following it
gets the error the README tells them to expect, so it does not mislead in practice.

NOTE, carried from QA1, not re-tested as a defect: the "### Running the policy tests" recipe
still omits the export step. The new section says so, and Master Controller owns the
follow-up.
